abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) tumors with a high migration-to-proliferation ratio (D/k) are associated with treatment resistance, motivating the estimation of D/k from routine pre-treatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data and the investigation of mechanisms underlying its heterogeneity across patients. Unlike previous approaches based on nested spherical approximations of enhancing and non-enhancing tumor volumes, we incorporate the spatial arrangement of the enhancing and non-enhancing tumor regions by deriving a 1D tumor density distribution from their segmentations and fitting a 1D reaction-diffusion model to estimate D/k. We achieved an error of under 5% when comparing our method to synthetic density distributions and found excellent correlation with synthetic tumor segmentations (Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) = 0.996). We then evaluated associations between patient-specific D/k values and their clinical, transcriptomic, and radiomic features. When applied to 102 pre-treatment MRI scans from the Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) 2017 dataset, elevated D/k significantly correlated with reduced overall survival (log-rank p = 0.01), older age (p = 0.04), and a trend toward lower Karnofsky Performance Status (p = 0.059). In a subset of 91 patients with available microarray data, mesenchymal-like phenotypes consistently exhibited elevated D/k across three established molecular subtype classifications (p = 0.013, p = 0.055, and p = 0.127). Elastic Net regularization followed by overrepresentation analysis revealed an enrichment of glycosylation-related pathways among genes associated with D/k variability (p = 0.0123 and p = 0.0368). Furthermore, Multi-Omic Factor Analysis identified a radiomic factor correlated with D/k (r = 0.57, p = 4x10-9), with the highest-weighted features corresponding to smoothness of the non-enhancing tumor region on T2 and FLAIR.
